correctness.rationale: Averaging over within-class permutations and exchange of the first two classes preserves constraints and cannot increase the spectral norm. The four nonstationary eigenvalues on within-class contrasts, the A−B contrast and the AB−C contrast are 1−X−Y, 1−κY, 1−2X−Y and 1−(1+κ)Y. For fixed Y, T=1−Y: if X<2T/3 then T−X>T/3; if X>2T/3 then 2X−T>T/3. The best possible value for these two X-dependent constraints is uniquely achieved at X=2T/3 with value T/3. The positive sign of the AB−C contrast is dominated by 1−κY. The remaining envelope is max{1−κY,(1+κ)Y−1,(1−Y)/3} on [0,min(1,1/κ)]. The decreasing and increasing bounds cross at Y=max{2/(1+2κ),4/(4+3κ)}, with the optimal Y clipped to the right endpoint if necessary. Strict decrease before the crossing and strict increase after it yield uniqueness in Y, the four branches, and transition points κ=1/2,2,4. For fixed optimal Y and μ, all feasible X lie in [max(0,1−Y−μ), min(1−Y,(1−Y+μ)/2)], giving exactly the stated face, including collapse at the two endpoints. At p=q (κ=2), the unique weights are equal across all three pairs, so the optimizer also respects the full automorphism group in that case. RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected; the reported finite rational LP and eigenvector checks were not rerun. No unrestricted optimizer classification beyond existence and value is inferred from averaging.
